classification.habitat: Forests, scrub and open woodland in tropical and subtropical regions
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in India and neighbouring South/Southeast Asian regions

identification.description: A woody climber with simple alternate leaves and distinctive yellow-orange arils surrounding seeds in mature capsules.
identification.whole_plant: Woody climber or scrambling shrub, often supported by surrounding vegetation.
identification.root: Woody root system; not a primary field character.
identification.stem: Woody, branched climbing stems, often with grey-brown bark when mature.
identification.leaf: Simple alternate leaves, generally elliptic to obovate with a serrated margin.
identification.flower: Small greenish-yellow flowers borne in axillary or terminal clusters.
identification.fruit: Capsule that opens when mature to expose seeds surrounded by a bright yellow-orange aril.
identification.seed: Hard seeds partly enclosed by a conspicuous orange-yellow aril; this is a useful recognition character.
identification.bark: Grey-brown bark on mature woody stems.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Seeds contain a fixed oil and diverse secondary metabolites. Exact marker compounds and concentrations vary by source and extraction method and should be verified from primary literature or pharmacopoeial material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Celastrus paniculatus has a long traditional history in Ayurveda and has been investigated experimentally for neurological and other effects. Experimental findings should not be presented as established human clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Seed oil is concentrated material; verify identity, preparation and dose from authoritative references before clinical use.

exam_points: Seed/oil is the listed useful part
Mature capsule exposes orange-yellow arillate seeds
viva_questions: What is the botanical name of Jyotishmati?
Which family does it belong to?
What is distinctive about the mature fruit and seed?
Which part is listed as useful?
mnemonics: Jyotishmati = Malakangni: remember the bright aril around the seed.
student.quick_revision: Jyotishmati (Celastrus paniculatus) is a woody climber of Celastraceae; seed/oil is listed as useful and the orange-yellow aril is a key identification feature.

teaching_points: Demonstrate the distinctive arillate seed as a practical identification feature.
Discuss why seed oil and crude seed should not be treated as interchangeable preparations.
discussion_points: Traditional Medhya description versus modern experimental evidence
practical_points: Observe mature capsule opening and aril colour.
Record leaf margin and climbing habit before sampling reproductive material.

doctor.quick_reference: Jyotishmati — Celastrus paniculatus Willd.; seed/oil is the useful part listed in the project record and traditional indications include Smritidaurbalya and Vata-related disorders.
key_precautions: Use authenticated seed and clearly identified preparation.
Do not infer dose from experimental studies or culinary use.
Verify formulation-specific safety before clinical use.
